description:
Space Uai is a team from Ouro Preto, Brazil: statistics, design, code, environmental engineering, veterinary medicine and audiovisual. We built De Olho no Fogo, which merges NASA's two fire sensors point by point and counts each fire once.

Time de Ouro Preto com estatística, design, código, engenharia ambiental, veterinária e audiovisual. Fizemos o De Olho no Fogo: junta os dois sensores de fogo da NASA ponto a ponto e conta cada fogo uma vez.
summary: MODIS (since 2000, 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (since 2012, 375 m pixels) see fire differently: one large fire lights several VIIRS pixels inside one MODIS pixel, is seen again on the next overpass, and small fires are seen by VIIRS only. Adding both lists counts the same fire several times, and switching from one to the other creates a false jump in 2012. De Olho no Fogo ("Eye on the Fire") harmonizes the two NASA FIRMS records point by point on the MODIS 1 km grid: every detection goes to its local solar day and its grid cell, and touching cells on the same day become one harmonized fire, labelled seen by both sensors, MODIS only or VIIRS only. In 2025, 20.5 million detections worldwide became 7.26 million harmonized fires; Brazil has a comparable series from 2000 to 2025. An interactive 3D globe lets anyone go from year to month, day and hour, and click a fire to see which satellites saw it, so fire managers, brigades and researchers can compare years fairly instead of reading a sensor change as a change on the ground.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. A web app with an interactive 3D globe and a method page, in plain language for anyone and with a "For nerds" switch that opens the full science. Globe layers: harmonized fires (on by default), raw MODIS, raw VIIRS, fixed heat sources (volcanoes, industry, offshore; 31,780 sites in 2025, kept out of the count) and burn scars for Brazil. Timeline from year to month, day and hour, in local solar time. Click a fire to see its cells, which satellites saw it and when.

METHODOLOGY. (1) Input: NASA FIRMS archive files, MODIS Collection 6.1 (Terra and Aqua, 1 km) and VIIRS S-NPP (375 m), all confidence levels, type 0 (vegetation fire) only; types 1-3 go to a separate fixed-source layer. (2) Local solar day: local time = UTC + longitude / 15 h, so night and afternoon overpasses of one place fall on the same day. (3) One grid: every detection is placed on the MODIS 1 km sinusoidal grid (R = 6,371,007.181 m, cell = 926.625 m); MODIS pixels wider than 1 km at the swath edge also occupy the cells under their footprint. (4) One fire: occupied cells that touch (8 neighbours) on the same local day form one harmonized fire, whatever the sensor or overpass, with a sheared-grid neighbour lookup. (5) Traceable: each fire keeps its cells, satellites, first and last time, largest FRP per sensor and raw detections, labelled both / MODIS only / VIIRS only. (6) Long series: MODIS-only fires are the ruler since 2000; before February 2012 Brazil's full total = MODIS-only fires x a monthly factor fitted on 2012-2021 (2.62-3.74).

RESULTS. World 2025: 3,502,268 MODIS + 17,014,675 VIIRS detections became 7,260,823 harmonized fires (12.4% seen by both, 11.9% MODIS only, 75.6% VIIRS only). Brazil 2025: 359,392. Validation of the long series by leaving one year out: median error 3.35% per year, 6.38% per month.

CHECKS AND EXTRAS (beyond the challenge resource). Against MODIS burned area (MCD64A1, via Google Earth Engine) the monthly correlation is 0.84: our number counts fire events, not burned area. Land-cover factors (MCD12C1) gave no gain, so one factor is kept. Cloud flags (MOD09GA) show how much fire clouds can hide (an upper bound, not applied). S-NPP stopped on 2 Nov 2026; NOAA-20 carries the series with a 0.976 bridge factor (median error 1.03% per year). NASA POWER daily weather for Brazil (2,454 cells, 2000-2025) feeds a fire-chance model that is still in progress.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY. Most conversions apply a factor to totals; ours can be checked fire by fire, because every number on the map leads back to the detections that formed it. It is built for fire managers, brigades, civil defense, conservation-unit managers and researchers who need to compare years fairly, and for anyone curious about fire near home. Next step: a fire-chance alert for recent fires.

TOOLS. Python 3 and NumPy (deterministic, reproducible processing from public FIRMS files), Next.js 16 and React 19 (website, automatic English/Portuguese by browser language with a PT/EN switch), MapLibre GL JS and deck.gl (3D globe), Google Earth Engine (validation), HyperFrames (30-second video).

LINKS. 7-slide pitch (interactive, with PDF and PPTX downloads): https://deolhonofogo.estudiocrivy.com.br/pitch?lang=en . 30-second video: https://deolhonofogo.estudiocrivy.com.br/pitch/De-Olho-no-Fogo-30s.mp4 . Open source code and data scripts: https://github.com/WednyFernandes/de-olho-no-fogo

LIMITS. Hot spots are not burned area nor confirmed wildfires; clouds and smoke hide fires; global point-level coverage is 2025 (other years are being processed); a fire crossing 180 degrees longitude becomes two.
